method: Manual adversarial construct-level comparison of every candidate against its highest-similarity canonical item after whole-bank screening; lexical overlap alone is not accepted as proof of distinctness.

comparisons.reason: Q1607 tests SLC52A2/riboflavin uptake and downstream FMN/FAD availability. Q1621 tests SLC19A2/THTR1-mediated thiamine uptake. Shared transporter/vitamin language does not represent the same substrate, gene, cofactor system, or tested mechanism.

Q0606 tests primary mitochondrial complex-I dysfunction in LHON from MT-ND variants. Q1622 tests ETHE1-dependent sulfide detoxification with secondary cytochrome-c-oxidase inhibition. Primary respiratory-chain subunit disease and toxic-metabolite-mediated COX inhibition are different constructs.

Q0838 tests PMM2 conversion of mannose-6-phosphate to mannose-1-phosphate and impaired N-linked oligosaccharide precursor synthesis. Q1623 tests SLC39A8 manganese deficiency causing reduced manganese-dependent Golgi beta-1,4-galactosyltransferase activity and abnormal glycan processing.

Q1617 tests citrin/SLC25A13-mediated metabolite exchange across the inner mitochondrial membrane. Q1624 tests AGK as a kinase-independent TIM22-complex subunit required for protein import and assembly of mitochondrial carriers. Metabolite transport and carrier-protein biogenesis are distinct.

Q0851 tests APRT purine salvage from adenine plus PRPP to AMP. Q1625 tests PANK2-catalyzed ATP-dependent phosphorylation of pantothenate in coenzyme-A biosynthesis. The common reaction-style lead does not create construct duplication.
